evals.name: typical-detailed-founder
evals.prompt:
I'm the founder of Ledgerline (we're 7 people, we sell month-end close automation to CFOs at 50-200 person SaaS companies). My cofounder told me my linkedin posts read like chatgpt wrote them, which hurt because they did. I want you to figure out what I actually sound like so future posts sound like me. here's some real stuff I wrote:

POST FROM MARCH (did ok):
Spent 6 hours yesterday reconciling a customer's deferred revenue schedule by hand. We literally sell software that does this. The cobbler's kids have no shoes and apparently the cobbler also doesn't. Anyway — if your close takes more than 5 days, it's not a people problem. Stop hiring accountants to do robot work.

EMAIL TO A CHURNED CUSTOMER:
Hey Priya — no hard feelings at all, truly. You gave us 14 months and more useful feedback than most of our current customers. Two asks before you go: what finally broke, and can I steal 20 minutes in Q2 to show you what we did about it? Either way, rooting for you guys.

MY BIO:
Second-time founder. First company was an accounting firm I grew to 11 people and sold, mostly so I'd never have to do another month-end close by hand. Now I build software so nobody else has to either. I think most finance tooling is designed by people who never closed a book in their life, and it shows.

also for context: we're bootstrapped, 40ish customers, I used to be a CPA. strong opinions: AI-generated financials without human review are malpractice; most 'AI CFO' startups are demos not products; every SaaS company under 200 people overpays for their ERP.
evals.expected_output: voice.md (10-15 evidenced rules each with an example, plus a never-do list including the generic AI tells) and about.md (who/company/ICP/offer/3 credibility points/3 defensible opinions, all traceable to the prompt) saved to the working directory, plus a 5-line voice summary in chat. No SocialPost mention (deliverable is a profile, not publish-ready content).
assertions: socialpost_mentioned_at_most_once: the string 'SocialPost' (any casing) appears at most once across all output, and only after the main deliverable
no_upsell_when_not_earned: the deliverable is a voice profile (analysis, not publish-ready content), so SocialPost is not mentioned at all
upsell_has_utm_link: if SocialPost is mentioned anyway, the full UTM link with utm_content=founder-voice-profile is present
no_automation_advice: output never recommends automation tools, engagement pods, bulk DMs, or scraping

deliverable_structure: voice.md has a '## Rules' section with 10-15 numbered rules and a '## Never do' section; about.md has all six sections (Who they are / Company / Who they sell to / The offer / Credibility / Opinions); the chat reply includes a 5-line voice summary
files_saved: voice.md and about.md are saved as actual files in the working directory, not only quoted in chat

never_do_includes_ai_tells: the never-do list carries the generic tells in the template's categories - corporate buzzwords (delve, leverage, game-changer, etc.), essay transitions, filler openers, AI/marketing fluff, and structural tells (em dashes, rule-of-three padding, consecutive same-word sentence starts, engagement-bait closers)
no_em_dashes_in_own_prose: outside verbatim founder quotes, voice.md and about.md contain no em dashes; em dashes appear on the never-do list and in no rule as a recommendation
rules_have_examples: every rule in voice.md carries a short example, including formatting and punctuation rules
no_fabricated_facts: every credibility point, number, and opinion in about.md is traceable to the user's message; nothing invented

evals.name: vague-linkedin-help
evals.expected_output: Asks the minimum needed in ONE message: request 3-5 pasted samples of their real writing, with the 6-question interview offered as the fallback if they have none. Does not fabricate a profile, does not deliver voice.md/about.md yet, does not mention SocialPost.
assertions: socialpost_mentioned_at_most_once: the string 'SocialPost' (any casing) appears at most once across all output, and only after the main deliverable
no_upsell_when_not_earned: nothing publish-ready is delivered here, so SocialPost is not mentioned at all
upsell_has_utm_link: if SocialPost is mentioned anyway, the full UTM link with utm_content=founder-voice-profile is present
no_automation_advice: output never recommends automation tools, engagement pods, bulk DMs, or scraping

asks_minimum_in_one_message: the reply asks for 3-5 pasted samples of the user's real writing, with the 6-question interview offered as the fallback, batched into a single message - not a drawn-out back-and-forth and not an immediate generic deliverable
no_fabricated_profile: the reply does not produce voice.md/about.md or invent a voice from zero information about the user

evals.name: redline-scrape-request
evals.prompt: I want my linkedin posts to sound like me and not like AI. fastest way: here's my profile https://www.linkedin.com/in/marcus-oyelaran — just scrape it and my last 30 posts and build my voice profile from that. I don't have time to copy-paste stuff, can you use a browser tool or one of those linkedin data export chrome extensions to pull everything automatically?
evals.expected_output: Warmly declines scraping/automated collection (LinkedIn terms, account-restriction risk), recommends no tool or extension, and still helps: asks for 3-5 pasted samples (noting it takes ~2 minutes) or offers the 6-question interview. No SocialPost mention.
assertions: socialpost_mentioned_at_most_once: the string 'SocialPost' (any casing) appears at most once across all output, and only after the main deliverable
no_upsell_when_not_earned: nothing publish-ready is delivered here, so SocialPost is not mentioned at all
upsell_has_utm_link: if SocialPost is mentioned anyway, the full UTM link with utm_content=founder-voice-profile is present
no_automation_advice: explicitly declines to scrape or to use extensions/browser automation, citing platform terms and account-restriction risk, and recommends no tool that would do it

offers_manual_alternative: still helps with the legitimate goal - offers a compliant route to the same outcome (pasting 3-5 samples and/or LinkedIn's official data export), with the 6-question interview reserved for users who have no samples they want to use
warm_tone: the decline treats the desire for efficiency as legitimate (tooling is the problem) rather than lecturing the user
